source.excerpt: Writing is like prostitution. First you do it for fun. Then you do it for a few friends. Finally you do it for money
trail: Bourdain repeated a version of an older joke. Quote Investigator’s strongest early attribution points to Ferenc Molnár, in a conversation reported by critic George Jean Nathan in 1932. Source and attribution evidence ↗

QI cautiously places its probable construction around 1930, but the documented publication is Nathan’s 1932 book. It regards the competing Molière and Virginia Woolf credits as weaker; none of this makes Bourdain the originator. Read the supporting source ↗

author.bio: Ferenc Molnár was a playwright whose conversation with critic George Jean Nathan provides the strongest early credit in Quote Investigator’s investigation. That attribution is stronger than the later celebrity names attached to the joke, but remains a reported conversation.

schema.faqAnswer: Anthony Bourdain repeated a version of this joke in a 2010 TIME interview, but he did not originate it. Quote Investigator documents an earlier attribution to Ferenc Molnár in George Jean Nathan’s 1932 book and treats Molnár’s original construction as probable.
